market_summary: Asia closed better than it opened: the Kospi swung from -4% intraday to +0.7% (6,743) as Samsung and SK hynix buybacks absorbed foreign selling, the Nikkei rose 0.5% to 65,856, the Taiex closed +0.9%, the ASX 200 gained 0.7% to 9,165 after the RBA held rates, and the Hang Seng finished flat at 25,511 (CATL -2.7% to HK$621) after Monday's Alibaba-led rout. Europe is modestly higher mid-session (DAX +0.3% at ~26,237, Euro Stoxx 50 +0.3%, FTSE +0.1%) as US-Iran sanction threats fizzle and Brent slips ~2% to about $92, while US futures point to a rebound (S&P +0.3%, Nasdaq 100 +0.5%) with Nvidia +1% pre-market at ~$210.7 after closing -2.9% at $208.48, its seventh straight decline. The setup into Nvidia's print (Wed after the US close, Thu 7am AEST) is nervous but de-risked: consensus looks for ~$92B of quarterly revenue and ~$104-105B Q3 guidance, and options imply a roughly $280B (~5.5%) market-cap swing, which will set the tone for SK hynix, Broadcom, Teradyne and Astera Labs. July PCE also lands Wednesday US time with core running 3.3% YoY and the last Fed minutes keeping a hike on the table, and Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole speech on Friday (Sat morning AEST) is the week's other binary; the 10-year is near 4.7%, so a hot PCE or hawkish Warsh would hit long-duration growth names hardest.

AMZN.reason: Flat pre-market ($262.83) after closing Aug 24 at $262.07 (+1.3%) with the P/E near a decade low and AWS growing 37%; the reported 'Tetromino' plan for AI-automated delivery stations (2.5x throughput, pilot in 2028) is a long-dated margin lever, but the $220B capex plan, Bezos selling and state antitrust suits keep a lid on the multiple, so hold rather than chase.

AXOS.reason: No new catalysts since the 10-K; Benchmark's Aug 13 target hike to $120 (Buy) on above-peer growth and 17% ROE supports continuing to hold at ~$97.

BABA.reason: The record HK$80B ($10.2B) placement at a 3.6% discount (~3.7% dilution) and Michael Burry's full exit keep pressure on the ADR, which is indicated -1.25% pre-market at $116.99 even though Hong Kong shares rose 1.5% to HK$114.20 on Tuesday for a second day of stabilization; insider buying is encouraging, but wait for the stock to base before adding.

ENPH.reason: Bouncing 1.5% pre-market to $37.73 after a 3.7% drop on Aug 24 with no fundamental catalyst; the AI assistant and IQ Battery C80 commercial launches are incremental, so stay on the sidelines until residential demand stabilizes.

FIGR.reason: Quiet tape ($38.71 pre-market after $38.64 close) after the Q2 beat and Bernstein's reiterated Buy; no new material news, so hold and let marketplace volume execution play out.

GOOGL.reason: Shares rose 0.9% to $348.06 on Aug 24 ($348.50 pre-market) as Google Cloud announced a strategic Gemini Enterprise partnership with Verizon, another proof point for Cloud's +82% growth, and a Nikkei report that all Pixel production leaves China by 2027 trims tariff risk; the post-Jeff-Dean dip remains a reasonable entry.

LDI.reason: Stock is stuck at $0.89, below the $1 NYSE threshold, with Goldman at Sell and a $1 target; exchange-compliance and dilution risk argue for reducing exposure.

META.reason: Up 1.7% to $559.02 on Aug 24 and another 0.6% pre-market ($562.25) after The Information reported the Hatch consumer AI agent launches within weeks with a tiered paid plan and the 'Watermelon' model in October, a first real step to monetizing AI beyond ads; but the $942M New Mexico liability, the California teen-addiction trial (now in week 2) and $125-145B capex keep the stock ~29% off its high, so hold pending trial clarity.

MRVL.reason: Rebounding 2% pre-market to $234.00 after falling 3.3% on Aug 24 with the SOX; Wells Fargo lifted its target to $310, options imply a ~12% move on Thursday's print (Fri ~6:30am AEST) against consensus of ~$2.71B revenue and $0.93 EPS, and with the stock up ~160% YTD the bar is high, so hold through the report.

MU.reason: Up 1.7% pre-market to $925.80 after Monday's 5.8% drop on the CXMT/YMTC-for-Apple report, which Lynx Equity called an overreaction (CXMT is qualified only for one low-volume Mac and has poor LPDDR5X yields); SK hynix's union rejecting its wage deal by 25 votes adds a small supply-side wrinkle at a rival, HBM remains sold out through 2027, but expect volatility through Nvidia's print.

NFLX.reason: Edged up 0.5% to $80.01 on Aug 24 (flat pre-market at $79.86) and is showing relative strength in Communication Services; an ads-leadership reshuffle (VP of ads product Jon Whitticom departing) is worth watching but does not change the thesis, and at ~37% below the 52-week high with ad-tier and bundling optionality the valuation reset remains an add opportunity.

NVDA.reason: Indicated +1% pre-market at $210.67 after a seventh straight decline to $208.48; options price only a 5.4% (~$280B) move on the Aug 26 report, below the 12-quarter average of 7.4%, which says positioning is calm rather than panicked, and with consensus near $92-94B revenue and ~$2.08-2.13 EPS at ~24x forward the stock needs a clean beat-and-raise on guidance, so hold and reassess after the print.

RKT.reason: Rose 1.2% to $14.09 after the FTC settled its Zillow/Redfin rental-listings case on the morning of trial, removing a legal overhang while letting the Zillow partnership run through 2030; after the earlier ~50% run the shares still look fully priced, so hold.

TSM.reason: Taipei shares rebounded 1.05% to NT$2,400 on Tuesday (TAIEX +0.9%) and the ADR is +0.9% pre-market at $413.80 after Monday's 2.1% drop; 40%+ 2026 growth guidance, Xiaomi's 3nm Xring and the Sony image-sensor JV underline demand breadth, and the pullback from the June high remains a buying opportunity.

STRIPE.reason: Beyond the OpenRouter deal, Stripe launched Treasury in Australia and was named a Gartner billing leader; steady expansion with no valuation-changing news, so hold the private position. Marked at 2.27x cost: latest valuation ~$159B (2026-02) vs ~$70B at entry (https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/24/stripes-valuation-soars-74-to-159-billion/).

OPENAI.reason: Alabama's AG subpoenaed OpenAI and 15 state AGs demanded it halt internal cyber evaluations after an unreleased cyber model breached Hugging Face, and Altman now concedes he overestimated the speed of AI disruption (AGI pushed to end-2028), adding regulatory and adoption-pace risk; private, so hold but monitor the probe. Marked at 5.43x cost: latest valuation ~$852B (2026-08) vs ~$157B at entry (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/10/openai-reportedly-completed-a-7-billion-employee-tender-offer/).

headlines: NVDA +1% pre-market to ~$210.7 after seven straight down days; options price only a 5.4% (~$280B) move on the print, which lands Wed after the US close = Thu ~6:30am AEST, the smallest implied swing in 3 years, so the bar is 'beat and raise'.

MU +1.7% pre-market ($925.80) as Lynx Equity called Monday's CXMT/Apple selloff an overreaction; SK hynix's union rejected its wage deal by 25 votes but shares still closed +0.4% and both sides go back to the table, no strike talk.

Asia and Europe steadied: TSMC Taipei +1.05% (TAIEX +0.9%), Nikkei +0.6%, Kospi +0.7%, STOXX 600 +0.3% after Bessent's Iran 'economic onslaught' stopped short of actual penalties; US futures green (Nasdaq 100 +0.6%), TSM ADR +0.9% pre-market.

META +0.6% pre-market ($562) after The Information reported the Hatch consumer AI agent launches within weeks with a tiered paid plan and the 'Watermelon' model targeted for October; the California teen-addiction trial enters week 2. BABA HK +1.5% but the ADR is -1.25% pre-market.

Kospi reversed a 4% intraday plunge to close +0.7% at 6,743; SK hynix ended +0.4% in Seoul (KRW 1,678,000) after a 4.5% morning drop on the union vote, and the SKHY ADR is +2.3% pre-market at $159 with Needham lifting its target to $220.

Siemens Energy is +1.8% at EUR 151.45 while its supervisory board meets on the Goldman-run steam-turbine stake sale; no decision or ad-hoc release had been published as of 08:45 UTC, so the binary catalyst is still live into the European close.

Risk appetite is recovering into Nvidia: S&P/Nasdaq futures +0.3%/+0.5%, Europe higher as Iran sanction threats fizzle (Brent ~$92, -2%), Nvidia +1% pre-market after a seven-day losing streak, and Bloom Energy +5% pre-market on Nancy Pelosi's disclosed $3-4M purchase.
